title: Block Distracting Apps at Bedtime on iPhone
description: Use a recurring app-blocking schedule to restrict selected distractions at bedtime.
direct: Use a recurring app-blocking schedule to restrict selected distractions at bedtime. A daily usage allowance answers a different question: how long you can use an app, rather than which hours it should be unavailable.
figureAlt: A face-down phone, book and bedside clock illustrate a scheduled overnight break.

cards.choice.heading: Start with one routine
cards.choice.body: Choose the apps that keep you scrolling and a realistic bedtime window. Keep essential communication and any overnight tasks in mind before selecting what to restrict.
sections.explain.heading: Understand the available exits
sections.explain.body: The app offers temporary unlocks of 5, 15 or 30 minutes. A schedule is therefore a practical friction tool, not a claim that every bypass is impossible. Its separate Block Now feature starts a 30-minute focus session; use that for a one-off break rather than treating it as the nightly recurring rule.
sections.practice.heading: Native option and app limits
sections.practice.body: Apple Screen Time also offers scheduled Downtime; check its blocking setting rather than assuming a reminder prevents continued use. Our iPhone app includes one scheduled rule and unlimited Block Now sessions free; Pro adds unlimited scheduled rules. Space Sheep Studio develops Dying Soon. Its optional life grid uses your chosen birthday and lifespan setting for reflection, not a health forecast. Notifications are optional and are not needed to define this bedtime routine.

steps.step-1.text: In Dying Soon: Screen Time Limit, grant the requested Apple Screen Time access and choose the distracting apps.
steps.step-2.text: Create a recurring schedule for your bedtime routine. Check its selected days and start/end times.
steps.step-3.text: Test the selected apps during the window and review the next morning. Adjust the routine if it blocks something you need.
